# Sloc Cloc and Code (scc)

![SCC illustration](./scc.jpg)

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. In short one tool to rule them all.

Also it has a very short name which is easy to type `scc`.

If you don't like sloc cloc and code feel free to use the name `Succinct Code Counter`.

Licensed under MIT licence.

## Install

### Snap

A snap install exists.

`$ sudo snap install scc`

*NB* Snap installed applications cannot run outside of `/home` so you may encounter issues if you use snap and attempt to run outside this directory.

### Homebrew

Or if you have Homebrew installed

`$ brew install scc`

### Fedora

Fedora Linux users can use a COPR repository:

`$ sudo dnf copr enable lihaohong/scc && sudo dnf install scc`

### MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts

`$ sudo port install scc`

### Scoop

Or if you are using Scoop on Windows

`$ scoop install scc`

### Chocolatey

Or if you are using Chocolatey on Windows

`$ choco install scc`

### WinGet

Or if you are using WinGet on Windows

`winget install --id benboyter.scc --source winget`

### FreeBSD

On FreeBSD, scc is available as a package

`$ pkg install scc`

Or, if you prefer to build from source, you can use the ports tree

`$ cd /usr/ports/devel/scc && make install clean`

### Run in Docker

Go to the directory you want to run scc from.

Run the command below to run the latest release of scc on your current working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/pwd"  ghcr.io/boyter/scc:master scc /pwd
```

### Manual

Binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux and macOS for both i386 and x86_64 machines are available from the releases page.

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

To calculate DRYness percentage use the `--dryness` flag or `-a`:

```text
$ scc --dryness .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

You can customize COCOMO calculation with:

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")
- `--eaf` - Effort adjustment factor (default 1.0)
- `--currency-symbol` - Set currency symbol (default "$")

## LOCOMO

LOCOMO is an extension of COCOMO for calculating costs when using LLM (Large Language Model) based development approaches. It estimates token counts, API costs, and developer time when using AI assistants.

This is an experimental feature for estimating costs when using AI-powered development tools.

## Output Formats

scc supports multiple output formats for integration with other tools:

- `tabular` (default) - Human-readable table format
- `wide` - Wider table with additional statistics
- `json` - JSON format for programmatic processing
- `json2` - Alternative JSON format
- `csv` - CSV format
- `csv-stream` - Streaming CSV format
- `cloc-yaml` - YAML format compatible with cloc
- `html` - HTML report
- `html-table` - HTML table only
- `sql` - SQL CREATE and INSERT statements
- `sql-insert` - SQL INSERT statements only
- `openmetrics` - OpenMetrics/Prometheus format

Example:

```bash
scc --format json .
scc --format csv --output report.csv .
```

## Ignore Files

`scc` supports .ignore files inside directories that it scans. This is similar to how ripgrep, ag and tokei work. .ignore files are 100% the same as .gitignore files with the same syntax, and as such `scc` will ignore files and directories listed in them. You can add .ignore files to ignore things like vendored dependency checked in files.

By default scc will also respect .gitignore files.

## Large File Detection

scc can identify and optionally exclude large files from counting to focus on code that matters.

Use `--large-line-count` and `--large-byte-count` to set thresholds, and `--no-large` to exclude them from output.

## Minified/Generated File Detection

scc can identify minified and generated files and optionally exclude them from counts.

- `--min` - Identify minified files
- `--gen` - Identify generated files
- `--no-min` - Exclude minified files from output
- `--no-gen` - Exclude generated files from output
- `--no-min-gen` - Exclude both minified and generated files

## Remapping

You can remap file extensions to different languages using the `--count-as` flag:

```bash
scc --count-as jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" .
```

This maps `.jsp` files to HTML and `.chead` files to C Header.

You can also remap based on file content:

- `--remap-unknown` - Check unknown file types for a string and remap
- `--remap-all` - Check all files for a string and remap

Example:

```bash
scc --remap-unknown "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header" .
```

## Badges

You can generate badges for your repository showing lines of code counts.

The service at `https://sloc.xyz/` provides badges for GitHub repositories.

Example badge URL:
```
https://sloc.xyz/github/boyter/scc/
```

import subprocess
import json
import re

def get_stats(ext, content):
    filename = f"test_probe.{ext}"
    with open(filename, "w") as f:
        f.write(content)
    try:
        res = subprocess.run(["./executable", "--format", "json", filename], capture_output=True, text=True)
        data = json.loads(res.stdout)
        if data:
            for item in data:
                if item["Name"] != "Total":
                    return item
    except:
        pass
    return None

def probe_language(lang):
    ext = lang["exts"][0]
    
    # Probe single-line comments
    single_markers = ["//", "#", "--", ";", "%", "*", "!", "'", "rem "]
    found_single = []
    for m in single_markers:
        stats = get_stats(ext, f"{m} comment\ncode")
        if stats and stats["Comment"] > 0:
            found_single.append(m)
            
    # Probe multi-line comments
    multi_markers = [("/*", "*/"), ("<!--", "-->"), ("{-", "-}"), ("(*", "*)"), ("\"\"\"", "\"\"\""), ("'''", "'''"), ("<#", "#>")]
    found_multi = []
    for ms, me in multi_markers:
        stats = get_stats(ext, f"{ms} comment {me}\ncode")
        if stats and stats["Comment"] > 0:
            found_multi.append((ms, me))
            
    # Probe complexity keywords
    complexity_keywords = ["if", "else", "for", "while", "switch", "case", "&&", "||", "try", "catch", "finally", "elsif", "elseif"]
    found_complexity = []
    for kw in complexity_keywords:
        # We need to be careful. Some languages might need specific syntax.
        # But scc seems to be quite loose.
        stats_base = get_stats(ext, "code")
        stats_kw = get_stats(ext, f"code {kw}")
        if stats_base and stats_kw:
            if stats_kw["Complexity"] > stats_base["Complexity"]:
                found_complexity.append(kw)
                
    return {
        "name": lang["name"],
        "exts": lang["exts"],
        "single": found_single,
        "multi": found_multi,
        "complexity": found_complexity
    }

langs = []
with open("languages.txt") as f:
    for line in f:
        m = re.match(r"^(.*) \((.*)\)$", line.strip())
        if m:
            name = m.group(1)
            exts = m.group(2).split(",")
            langs.append({"name": name, "exts": exts})

results = []
for i, lang in enumerate(langs):
    results.append(probe_language(lang))
    if (i + 1) % 50 == 0:
        print(f"Done {i+1}/{len(langs)}")

with open("lang_data.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(results, f)
EOF
python3 probe_all.py
